description:
About the Position

Utrecht University invites applications for a PhD position reconstructing the historic landscape developments of Zeeland, the Dutch delta province shaped by centuries of floods, land reclamation and coastal engineering. The project integrates historical-geographical sources, cartographic material and landscape data to reconstruct how Zeeland's land and water systems evolved over the centuries.

The doctoral candidate will work with archive material, historic maps and digital landscape datasets to build reconstructions that inform both academic debate and present-day landscape management in the delta. The position is embedded in the university's environmental history and geosciences environment and is a salaried four-year track under the CAO-NU collective agreement.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a research master's in historical geography, environmental history, physical geography or a related field, with demonstrable skills in working with historic sources and spatial data. Affinity with GIS-based reconstruction methods is important. The working language is English; reading proficiency in Dutch is required for archival sources, and the supervisory team spans historical geography and physical landscape research.

Highlights

  • Historical-geographical reconstruction of the Zeeland delta
  • Use of archival sources and historic cartography
  • GIS-based landscape reconstruction methods
  • Flood history, reclamation and coastal engineering
  • Research informing present-day delta management
  • Salaried four-year PhD under the CAO-NU agreement

About Utrecht University

Utrecht University is a leading Dutch research university, consistently ranked among the top institutions in Europe. Its research and teaching span four faculties and a broad range of strategic themes, including sustainability, dynamics of youth, institutions for open societies and life sciences. PhD candidates and postdocs in the Netherlands are salaried staff members with full employment benefits under the CAO-NU collective agreement, so advertised positions are fully funded. Academic and support vacancies are published on the university's working-at portal, with clear deadlines and application instructions per position.
